sessions.session_summary: Session 1 grounded the PWA mental model in StudyElf (learner's real pharmacy education app). Key breakthrough: learner walked through their actual apiClient.ts and flashcard session code to evaluate PWA fitness. Discovered their 'use client' architecture, REST conventions, and existing FlashcardReview event log are all favorable for PWA. Built the three-layer model: service worker intercepts (cache reads via GET, queue writes via POST), local storage (Cache API + IndexedDB), background sync (event replay on reconnect). Drew smart scope boundary: student study flows offline, instructor/admin online-only. Open questions for next session: SW lifecycle phases, caching strategy selection (five flavors), quiz answer security in offline mode, Next.js-specific PWA tooling.
sessions.grounding_context: Used learner's StudyElf V3 codebase throughout — flashcard session page, apiClient.ts, FlashcardReview endpoint, architecture doc. This real-app grounding was extremely effective.

topics_covered.notes: Full lifecycle understanding achieved: install → wait → activate → fetch → update. Byte-diff trigger, 24hr auto-check, skipWaiting concept. Initially conflated SW update with per-request caching but self-corrected after clarification. Understands waiting state protects mid-session users.

Mapped all five caching strategies to StudyElf resource types with correct reasoning. Cache-first for hashed assets, SWR for HTML shells, network-first for analytics dashboards, cache-only for content packs. Key insight: URL immutability (content hash) determines safe cache-first usage. Correctly identified cache-only failure mode for new users.

Traced full SSR → hydration → useEffect sequence. Connected to standalone vs export: server only produces empty shells for 'use client' components. This is the architectural insight that unlocked the export migration discovery.

Explored CDN caching vs SW caching interaction. Initial intuition that cache-first ≈ SWR with CDN was corrected — understood cache-first never hits CDN for returning users. Good question about scale/performance tradeoffs showed curiosity.

Walked through complete offline flashcard scenario: answer (POST→queue), next card (GET→cache+client SM-2), performance history (GET→network-first fallback). Understood staleness cost varies by content type (history ok stale, pharmacology content not).

Major architectural discovery: standalone→export migration. Ran full codebase analysis confirming zero server features used. Identified elimination of Node.js container (1 CPU, 1 GB savings). CDN deployment unlocked. This emerged organically from PWA mental model questions.
Concrete migration analysis: 2 trivial code fixes, infrastructure config updates. Identified Cloudflare Pages as natural CDN fit. Understands NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL bake-time constraint.
Retrieval probe: correctly recalled event sourcing sync model. Applied in offline scenario: POST flashcard answer → IndexedDB queue.

sessions.session_summary: Session 2 completed TC-1 Foundations. Covered SW lifecycle (install→wait→activate→fetch→update, byte-diff trigger, skipWaiting), all five caching strategies mapped to StudyElf resource types, and the interaction between SW update cycle and per-request caching. Major architectural discovery: Next.js standalone→export migration — learner's codebase uses zero server features, so the Node.js container can be eliminated entirely. Covered CDN caching vs SW caching interaction. Final integration exercise: walked through complete offline flashcard scenario (POST queue, GET cache, network-first analytics). TC-1 mastery gate effectively passed — learner can articulate the three-layer model, map strategies to resource types, and reason about offline behavior for their specific app.
sessions.grounding_context: StudyElf V3 codebase, next.config.mjs output mode, standalone→export migration analysis, CDN deployment strategy

topics_covered.notes: Understood HTTP cache as middle layer. Initially skipped in pharmacology scenario but correctly integrated after prompting. Learned fetch({ cache: 'reload' }) bypass.
Strong retrieval on cache-first safety (content hash = URL immutability). Designed versioned cache naming and multi-cache architecture by purpose.
Clean retrieval of phases. Learned 24hr auto-check. Understood activate as cache cleanup moment. Found skipWaiting danger and first-install registration bug.
Correctly traced SW->CDN->origin path. Chose API-driven cache purging over TTLs for infrequent high-stakes updates. Full invalidation sequence mastered.

Key session learning. Initially missed HTTP cache layer in three-layer trace. Identified Cache-Control max-age as failure mode. Guessed header values before landing on fetch option. Missed in first Serwist plan draft but caught immediately when prompted.
Produced complete Serwist caching config: SWR for study content (500 entries/7d), NetworkFirst for API (64 entries/1d), CacheFirst for static via defaultCache. Correct route ordering.
Understood Workbox/Serwist abstraction. Caught next-pwa deprecation before building on stale tooling. Produced complete Serwist migration plan. Correct @serwist/next vs @serwist/turbopack decision.
Designed full update lifecycle: skipWaiting:false -> waiting state -> sonner toast -> SKIP_WAITING message -> controllerchange reload. Found first-install bug (controller gate).

Identified single-versioned-cache anti-pattern, stale tooling risk, skipWaiting for long sessions, first-install prompt bug. Missed fetchOptions in own plan — pattern matching improving but not yet automatic.

sessions.session_summary: Session 3 covered TC-2 Caching Deep Dive. Three-layer cache model (Cache API + HTTP cache + CDN) taught through pharmacology correction scenario. Key learning: fetch({ cache: 'reload' }) bypasses browser HTTP cache — initially missed, then internalized. Cache versioning: versioned names by purpose (static-vN, shell-vN, api-content, precached-packs), cleanup in activate handler. Serwist introduced as Workbox-fork for Next.js — learner caught next-pwa deprecation independently. Bulk of session spent reviewing and validating learner's Serwist migration plan for StudyElf. Found 5 issues across 2 review rounds: missing fetchOptions cache:reload, skipWaiting danger, window.serwist reliability, unbounded cache growth, first-install update prompt bug. All fixed in final plan. Self-assessed 3.5/5 — accurate calibration. Pattern-matching and assessment instincts strong; not yet automatic (missed fetchOptions in own plan despite just learning it).
sessions.grounding_context: Serwist migration plan for StudyElf PWA, ADR-013 Phase 4. Plan review as teaching vehicle was extremely effective — real stakes, real decisions.

curriculum_position.notes: Session 3 covered cache layer interactions, versioning, invalidation, Serwist tooling, and update flow design.
